feedback: Flag the four/for and 'thirteen'/'thirty' traps as they happen, contrasting the two spellings with their quantities.

If a young learner spells phonetically (e.g. 'fiveteen', 'elevin', 'nighn' for nine), treat it as normal early spelling: keep showing the correct written form and let spelling mature rather than marking it as a maths failure.
Praise correct production of irregular forms specifically, since these cannot be sounded out.
activities.intendedInsight: Reading a number word and producing its correct written form are different skills; learners need to spell the word, not only recognise it.
learnerActions: Look at a shown numeral (for example 13).
Use letter tiles, tracing, or handwriting to build or write the matching word ('thirteen').
Check the spelling against a reference wall, correcting classic traps like four/for and thirteen/thirty.
Spell several words one–twenty, returning to the irregular and teen forms for extra practice.
activities.title: Build-the-word: spell the number for a numeral

feedback: If a learner reads 'thirteen' as 31, re-point to the full ten plus three ones: the word means one ten and three, not three tens and one.
Contrast minimal pairs by sound and quantity: 'thirteen' vs 'thirty', 'fifteen' vs 'fifty', matching each to counters.
Confirm 'eleven' and 'twelve' by sight, since their letters give no clue to the quantity.
activities.intendedInsight: The teens name ten-and-ones even though the word is opaque ('eleven'/'twelve') or says the ones-part first; keeping the structure visible helps prevent the reversal 'thir-teen → 31'.
learnerActions: Segment each teen word from thirteen to nineteen beside its quantity: thir·teen, four·teen, fif·teen, and so on.
Place each segmented word next to a ten-frame showing one full ten plus the ones part.
Memorise 'eleven' and 'twelve' as sight words paired with their ten-and-ones frames.
Say the word slowly and match it to the quantity, noticing that the ones-word comes first (thir-) but the quantity is ten-and-three.
activities.title: Teen zone: keep ten-and-ones visible

feedback: If the wrong quantity appears after reading a word (e.g. 20 or 2 counters for 'twelve'), reteach the irregular word as a sight word alongside its numeral.
If a learner reads or writes the wrong member of a minimal pair (twelve/twenty), place the two words side by side with their quantities and say each slowly.
Confirm success when the learner acts on the word correctly and produces the word form, not merely when they recite a sequence.
activities.intendedInsight: Number words are used to act in the world: reading one to do something and producing a word label shows real command beyond reciting.
learnerActions: Read a short real instruction, e.g. 'buy twelve eggs', and set out that many counters, then write the numeral.
Label a box of 15 crayons with the number WORD.
Meet number words on a washing line 0–20, on classroom labels, and in books/rhymes repeatedly, not just in a maths drill.
Read a word to make or point to the quantity, and write the word for a given numeral.
activities.title: Number words in real reading and writing
